name: SilkParasite
akas: Unknown (Bitdefender declines firm attribution; notes tooling/infrastructure overlap with FamousSparrow/SneakyChef, medium-confidence China-nexus)
brief: Bitdefender Labs tracked a ~10-month Central Asian espionage campaign (Oct 2025 – Aug 2026) deploying seven RAT families, five previously undocumented, against government targets. Bitdefender assesses medium confidence that development was AI-assisted — not AI-generated — based on code artifacts: leftover AI-scaffolding test functions in GoginRAT, a hardcoded placeholder AES key (`0123456789abcdef`), a literal `change_this_key` placeholder in NodeEdgeRAT's config, and architectural similarity between a Go and a C++ implant that Bitdefender calls "not conclusive" but "the kind of thing an AI-assisted workflow makes easy." Separately, two recovered phishing lures — a fake regional energy-cooperation platform and a fake GPU cloud-computing advertisement — were themselves AI-generated. Bitdefender explicitly distinguishes this "AI-assisted development" evidence from a stronger "AI-generated malware" claim. Bitdefender *Analyst note: vendor report (Bitdefender sells EDR/endpoint security); China-nexus attribution and the SpiceRAT/SneakyChef/FamousSparrow overlap are all held at medium confidence by Bitdefender itself, so this row is NOT merged into the existing Salt Typhoon (FamousSparrow AKA) row pending firmer attribution.*
